question: Which conjunction best connects these two ideas: 'I wanted to play outside, ___ it started raining'? 🌧️
explanation: Great job! 'But' is a coordinating conjunction used to connect two contrasting or opposing ideas. You wanted to play, but the rain stopped you! 🛑
hint: Use the word that shows a contrast or a sudden change in plans.

question: What conjunction fits best here: 'She loves to read books, ___ she loves to write stories.'? 📚
explanation: Awesome! The word 'and' is used to add one idea to another similar idea. ➕
hint: We are adding two things she loves doing together.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I was very tired, ___ I went to bed early.' 🛌
explanation: Fantastic! 'So' shows a result or consequence. Because you were tired, the result was going to bed! ➡️
hint: Look for the word that shows the result of being tired.

question: Which conjunction gives a choice: 'Would you like to have tea ___ coffee?' ☕
explanation: Brilliant! The conjunction 'or' is used when we are presenting an alternative or a choice between two things. 🔀
hint: Think about picking one option over the other.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The movie was long, ___ it was very exciting.' 🎬
explanation: Spot on! 'Yet' is similar to 'but' and introduces a contrasting idea. Even though it was long, it was still exciting! ⏳
hint: This word shows a contrast, similar to 'but'.

question: Which of these words is the 'N' in the FANBOYS acronym? 🦸‍♂️
explanation: Excellent! The 'N' in the FANBOYS acronym stands for 'nor', which is used to present a second negative idea. 🛑
hint: It is used after 'neither'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I do not like spinach, ___ do I like broccoli.' 🥦
explanation: Great work! 'Nor' is used to continue a negative thought (not liking spinach, and not liking broccoli either). 🛑
hint: This is a negative word that often pairs with 'neither'.

question: What is the correct subordinating conjunction? 'We stayed inside ___ it was snowing heavily.' ❄️
explanation: Perfect! 'Because' tells us the reason why they stayed inside. 🧠
hint: This word answers the question 'Why?'

question: Choose the best connector: '___ it was raining, they still went for a walk.' ☔
explanation: Awesome! 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction that shows a contrast or unexpected result. 🤔
hint: It means 'even though'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'You can go to the party ___ you finish your homework first.' 🎒
explanation: Fantastic! 'If' introduces a condition that must be met before going to the party. ❓
hint: This word sets a condition for something to happen.

question: Which word completes the sentence: 'You won't pass the test ___ you study hard.' 📝
explanation: Brilliant! 'Unless' means 'except if'. You will not pass except if you study! 🚪
hint: It means 'if you do not'.

question: Fill in the blank: '___ I was sleeping, my cat knocked over a vase.' 🐈
explanation: Spot on! 'While' shows that two actions were happening at the exact same time. ⏳
hint: This word talks about time and things happening together.

question: Identify the conjunction: 'I will call you when I arrive.' 📞
explanation: Excellent! 'When' is the subordinating conjunction connecting the two clauses. ⏱️
hint: It is a word that refers to time.

question: Which conjunction shows a reason? '___ it is your birthday, I bought you a gift.' 🎁
explanation: Great job! 'Since' can be used just like 'because' to show a reason for an action. ⏱️
hint: It is similar in meaning to 'because'.

question: Which word partners with 'Either' to form a correlative conjunction? ⚖️
explanation: Awesome! 'Either' and 'or' always work together as a team to present two choices. 🔀
hint: Think of the phrase 'Either this ___ that'.

question: Which word partners with 'Neither' to form a correlative conjunction? ⚖️
explanation: Fantastic! 'Neither' and 'nor' pair up to show that both of two options are negative or not true. 🛑
hint: It starts with an 'N' just like 'Neither'.

question: Fill in the blanks: 'I will eat ___ the cake ___ the pie.' 🍰🥧
explanation: Brilliant! 'Either...or' is the correct correlative pair showing a choice between the two desserts! 🔀
hint: You have to choose one of the two options.

question: Complete the pair: '___ my brother and my sister are older than me.' 👨‍👩‍👧
explanation: Spot on! 'Both' pairs with 'and' to include two subjects together. 🤝
hint: This word means 'the two of them together'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'He is not only smart ___ very funny.' 😂
explanation: Excellent! 'Not only' always pairs up with 'but also' to add emphasis to two great qualities. ✨
hint: Think of adding something extra on top of the first thing.

question: Complete the correlative pair: 'I don't know ___ to stay or leave.' 🚪
explanation: Great work! 'Whether' pairs with 'or' when you are expressing a doubt or choice between two alternatives. 🤔
hint: It sounds like the weather outside, but spelled differently.

question: What type of conjunction is 'because'? 🧠
explanation: Awesome! 'Because' introduces a dependent (subordinate) clause, making it a subordinating conjunction. 🔗
hint: It connects a dependent clause to an independent clause.

question: What type of conjunctions are 'FANBOYS'? 🦸‍♂️
explanation: Fantastic! FANBOYS (For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So) are all coordinating conjunctions that link equal parts of a sentence. 🤝
hint: They coordinate or balance equal parts of a sentence.

question: Which of these is a pair of correlative conjunctions? 👯
explanation: Brilliant! Correlative conjunctions always work in pairs, like 'Either / Or'. 🔀
hint: Look for the pair that always travels together in sentences.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Please clean your room ___ we go to the park.' 🧹
explanation: Spot on! 'Before' tells us the timing of when the room needs to be cleaned. ⏱️
hint: This word deals with time and doing something first.

question: Fill in the blank: 'We can play video games ___ we finish our chores.' 🎮
explanation: Excellent! 'After' is a subordinating conjunction showing that the gaming happens later in time. ⏱️
hint: It means 'later than'.

question: Choose the best connector: 'I will wait here ___ you get back.' 🧍
explanation: Great job! 'Until' shows that the action of waiting continues up to the point when the person returns. ⏳
hint: It means 'up to the time that'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I saved my allowance ___ I could buy a new bike.' 🚲
explanation: Awesome! 'So that' explains the purpose or the goal of saving the allowance. 🎯
hint: It shows the purpose or reason behind an action.

question: Identify the correlative conjunction pair in this sentence: 'Both the dog and the cat are sleeping.' 😴
explanation: Fantastic! 'Both' and 'and' work together as a pair to connect two subjects in the sentence. 🤝
hint: Look for the two grammar words that are working as a team.

question: Which of these sentences uses a subordinating conjunction? 🔗
options: I will stay if it rains. 🌧️
Do you want tea or coffee? ☕
answer: I will stay if it rains. 🌧️
explanation: Brilliant! The word 'if' is a subordinating conjunction that creates a dependent clause. 🌧️
hint: Look for a sentence with a condition ('if').

question: Fill in the blank: 'I will follow you ___ you go.' 🗺️
explanation: Spot on! 'Wherever' connects the clauses by showing place or location. 📍
hint: This word relates to any place or location.

question: What is wrong with this sentence: 'I wanted to buy a toy, because I didn't have enough money.' 💸
explanation: Excellent! The two ideas are contrasting, so 'but' makes perfect sense here instead of 'because'. 🛑
hint: Look for the relationship between wanting a toy and not having money.

question: What does the 'S' stand for in FANBOYS? 🦸‍♂️
explanation: Great work! The 'S' in FANBOYS stands for the coordinating conjunction 'so'. ➡️
hint: It is a tiny two-letter word.

question: Which conjunction fills the blank: '___ I was running to catch the bus, I dropped my phone.' 📱
explanation: Awesome! 'While' introduces the action that was happening when another event interrupted it. ⏳
hint: It means 'at the same time as'.

question: Which conjunction shows contrast? ⚖️
explanation: Fantastic! 'Although' is used to introduce a contrasting or surprising idea. 🤔
hint: It means the same as 'even though'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'She won the race ___ she practiced every day.' 🏃‍♀️
explanation: Brilliant! 'Because' provides the reason for her winning the race. 🧠
hint: This answers 'why' she won.

question: Fill in the blanks: '___ Sarah ___ Tom knew the answer to the difficult question.' 🤷‍♀️🤷‍♂️
explanation: Spot on! 'Neither...nor' shows that not a single one of the two people knew the answer. 🛑
hint: Both people did not know it.

question: Which conjunction makes sense? 'He wore a thick coat ___ it was freezing outside.' 🧥
explanation: Excellent! 'Because' explains the reason for wearing a thick coat. 🧠
hint: Look for the cause and effect.

question: What is the conjunction in this sentence: 'I am tired yet I cannot sleep.' 🥱
explanation: Great job! 'Yet' acts as a coordinating conjunction here, showing a contrast similar to 'but'. ⏳
hint: It is one of the FANBOYS.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I will help you ___ long as you try your best.' 🌟
explanation: Awesome! 'As long as' is a subordinating conjunction phrase that sets a condition. 📏
hint: The phrase means 'on the condition that'.

question: Choose the best correlative pair: 'We can ___ eat pizza ___ have burgers.' 🍔🍕
explanation: Fantastic! 'Either...or' offers a clear choice between two dinner options! 🔀
hint: You have to choose one food.

question: Which of these words is NOT a coordinating conjunction? 🕵️‍♂️
explanation: Brilliant! 'Because' is a subordinating conjunction, not a coordinating one. It is not part of FANBOYS! 🧠
hint: Check the word against the FANBOYS acronym.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I enjoy swimming, ___ my brother prefers surfing.' 🌊
explanation: Spot on! 'But' shows the contrast between the two different preferences of the siblings. 🛑
hint: This word shows a difference in choices.

question: What type of conjunctions always come in pairs? 👯
explanation: Excellent! Correlative conjunctions like 'either/or' and 'both/and' always work in teams of two. 👯
hint: The word 'co' means together.

question: Which conjunction fits? 'You can't go to the park ___ you clean your room.' 🛏️
explanation: Great work! 'Unless' sets a rule that MUST be followed before going to the park. 🚪
hint: It means 'except if'.

question: Identify the conjunction: 'He failed the test for he did not study.' 📖
explanation: Awesome! 'For' is used here as a coordinating conjunction that means the same as 'because'. 🎁
hint: It is the 'F' in FANBOYS.

question: Complete the pair: '___ only did she bake a cake, ___ she also decorated it beautifully.' 🎂
explanation: Fantastic! 'Not only... but also' is a pair used to highlight two impressive actions. ✨
hint: Look for the pair that adds emphasis to the extra action.

question: Which connector shows time? ⏰
explanation: Brilliant! 'When' is a subordinating conjunction that tells us the specific time something happened. ⏱️
hint: Think about the hands on a clock.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I bought some flour ___ I can bake cookies later.' 🍪
explanation: Spot on! 'So that' gives us the purpose or reason behind buying the flour. 🎯
hint: It explains the final goal.

question: Which sentence has a correlative conjunction? 🔍
options: Neither my mom nor my dad knew. 🤷‍♂️
I cried because I was sad. 😢
answer: Neither my mom nor my dad knew. 🤷‍♂️
explanation: Excellent! 'Neither...nor' is a correlative conjunction pair used in that sentence. 🤷‍♂️
hint: Look for the sentence with a matching pair of conjunctions.

question: Fill in the blank: '___ the heavy rain, we still had a picnic.' 🧺
explanation: Great job! 'Despite' (or 'In spite of') is used to show that something happened even when there was a big obstacle! 🛡️
hint: This word shows that the rain did not stop the picnic.
